title: "Discussion"
---

**SiMR** (*Similarity-driven Multi-view Representation*) generalizes classical Similarity-driven Multi-view Linear Reconstruction (**SiMLR**) [@avants2021] around a single architectural invariant: every view $m$ enters through a linear loading matrix $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ regularized by Non-negative Stiefel Approximating Flow (`nsa_flow`) [@avants2025], while downstream consensus alignment, decoding (`LEND`), or density estimation (`Flow-SiMR-V`) may be linear or non-linear. Across 324 multi-seed evaluations on 12 datasets, a 1,214-configuration sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$), and 1,215 operating-point fits, this formulation preserves feature-level attribution in native measurement units while matching or exceeding unconstrained baselines depending on data geometry.

## When Multi-View SiMR Models Outperform Single-Matrix PCA—and Why PCA Often Suffices

A central practical question for clinical and translational investigators is when to use multi-view alignment versus single-matrix `PCA` or `NSAFlow-PCA`, and why linear probes often fail to separate them on simple cohorts. Two mechanisms govern this behavior:

1. **Subspace rotation invariance of linear regression probes:** Any invertible transformation $\mathbf{M} \in \mathrm{GL}(k, \mathbb{R})$ leaves $\operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}) = \operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m)$ unchanged. When a dataset has few features ($p \le 15$ in `Heart` and `Diabetes`) or when the shared disease signal already dominates the top principal components (`MultiOmics` ER status), `PCA` and `SiMR` span nearly the same $k$-dimensional subspace and therefore achieve similar linear prediction scores—even though `PCA` mixes all features densely while `SiMR` ($\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$) localizes them onto sparse, disjoint pathways.
2. **Rejection of view-private variance and bipartite supervision:** Multi-view SiMR outperforms `PCA` on predictive accuracy when individual views carry large view-private noise (`Shared+Private`, `NonnegPartsWeak`), when views differ sharply in dimensionality (`mfeat`), or when training aligns predictor views against a supervisory clinical battery withheld at deployment (`ADNI-MCI`).

@tbl-method-selection summarizes our empirical recommendations by data regime.

## Diagnostic Value of the Three Evaluation Probes

The 1,215-fit benchmark demonstrates that evaluating representations via a single linear regression probe introduces severe blind spots:

1. **Subspace Rotation Invariance (Linear Probe on $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$):** Ordinary least squares (OLS) regression on $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ is exactly invariant under orthogonal basis rotations: $\operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}\mathbf{R}) = \operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V})$ for any $\mathbf{R} \in \mathrm{O}(k)$. Consequently, the linear probe measures only whether the $k$-dimensional subspace contains the disease signal; it cannot detect whether coordinate 1 isolates a specific biological pathway or is an arbitrary 45-degree diagonal mixture of two unrelated pathways.
2. **Axis-Aligned Sensitivity (Random Forest Probe on $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$):** In contrast, decision tree ensembles perform axis-orthogonal splits ($z_j \le \theta$). When biological factors are diagonally rotated across axes, decision trees must construct complex staircases of splits across multiple variables, degrading generalization. On synthetic weak non-negative ground truth (`NonnegPartsWeak`), PCA achieves a linear probe score of $0.1246$ but collapses on the Random Forest probe to $-0.000053$ (effectively $0.0\%$), and on `ADNI-MCI`, PCA drops from $0.1522$ to $0.0441$. In contrast, SiMR architectures preserve single-axis alignment ($0.1969$ for `Flow-SiMR-V` on `ADNI-MCI`, $0.3855$ for `LEND` on `NonnegPartsWeak`). The Random Forest probe is indispensable for verifying that learned coordinates align with separable biological mechanisms.
3. **Cross-Modality Synthesis (Consensus Probe on $\mathbf{U}$):** The consensus probe tests whether multi-view representations compress into a unified cross-modal patient coordinate. Where sample sizes are limited, non-linear decoders (`LEND`, `Flow-SiMR-V`) succeed by keeping encoding linear and decoding non-linear, whereas post-projection deep encoders (`NED`, `NEDPP`) overfit and collapse (ranks $6.25$ and $7.12$).

## Clinical Operating Points: Balancing Systems Discovery ($q = 0.5$) vs. Focal Panel Design ($q = 0.8$)

The quantile `sparseness` parameter $q \in (0, 1)$ governs the sparsity-accuracy trade-off:

* **$q = 0.5$ (Balanced Systems Biology & Discovery):** Enforces $50\%$ sparsity per column ($41.3\%$ mean sparsity achieved). This operating point maximizes linear subspace fidelity ($0.6793$) and Random Forest axis interpretability ($0.6505$), outperforming unsparsified models ($q = \text{None}$) by removing diffuse noise. Recommended for exploratory multi-omics, connectomics, and whole-brain neuroimaging where polygenic or distributed network interactions (e.g., Default Mode Network) are anticipated.
* **$q = 0.8$ (Focal Diagnostic Biomarker Panel Design):** Enforces $80\%$ sparsity per column ($61.9\%$ mean sparsity achieved). On 80%-sparse ground truth (`NonnegPartsWeak`), $q = 0.8$ drives ground-truth support recovery to $F_1 = 0.710$ (vs. $0.482$ at $q = \text{None}$ ), and on `Shared+Private` to $F_1 = 0.797$ (vs. $0.540$), while retaining $99.1\%$ of unsparsified predictive power. Recommended when translating computational models into physical clinical assays—such as a 20-gene qPCR/NanoString panel or a brief 10-ROI MRI volumetric screening protocol.

## Role of the Approximate Stiefel Weight $w \in (0, 1)$, Positivity, Row-Mean Control, Quantile `sparseness`, and Rank $k$

Our basis-geometry ablations (@tbl-w-sweep, @tbl-rowmean-ica-ablation, @tbl-k-sparsity-sweep, @tbl-quantile-sparseness) clarify four rules governing the interpretability of $\mathbf{V}_m$:

1. **Why $w = 0.5$ balances rank preservation against combinatorial stiffness:** In `nsa_flow` [@avants2025], $w \in [0, 1]$ weights the normalized Stiefel defect $D(\mathbf{V}_m)$ against anchor fidelity $(1 - w)\mathcal{L}_{\text{fid}}$. On `ADNI-MCI` (@fig-w-sweep), setting $w < 0.20$ allows the cross-view gradient to pull columns together into rank collapse ($\operatorname{EffRank} = 2.02$ of $3$, $D = 0.244$ at $w = 0.01$). Conversely, pushing $w \to 0.95$ eliminates the anchor fidelity term, increasing wall-clock runtime $2.5\times\text{–}3.8\times$ and degrading out-of-sample `CogPC1` $R^2$ ($0.159 \to 0.132$) as iterates pin against combinatorial orthant vertices. The default $w = 0.50$ achieves full effective rank ($\operatorname{EffRank} = 3.00$, $D = 6.2 \times 10^{-4}$) and $64.8\%$ sparsity at less than half the runtime of $w = 0.95$.
2. **Positivity ($\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$) and the $1 - 1/k$ sparsity scaling:** Without positivity (`positivity="either"`) and with `sparseness=None`, Stiefel orthogonality is satisfied via signed cancellation with $0.0\%$ exact zeros (Stiefel defect $D \le 4.5 \times 10^{-5}$). Enabling $\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$ forces orthogonal columns onto nearly disjoint supports, where partitioning $p_m$ features across $k$ columns yields a theoretical sparsity baseline of $1 - 1/k$ ($50.0\%$ at $k=2$, $66.7\%$ at $k=3$, $80.0\%$ at $k=5$, $87.5\%$ at $k=8$, and $91.7\%$ at $k=12$).
3. **Why Component 1 ($\mathbf{v}_1$) is dense under un-thresholded PCA initialization, and two complementary remedies:** In neuroimaging and multi-omics cohorts, positive inter-regional correlations cause the first principal component $\mathbf{v}_1^{\text{PCA}}$ to act as an all-positive global size collector ($\bar{x}_{i,m} = \frac{1}{p_m}\sum_j X_{ij,m}$). Because $D(\mathbf{V}_m)$ penalizes only between-column overlap and norm imbalance, under standard column-centering and PCA initialization without quantile thresholding (`sparseness=None`), Component 1 remains relatively dense ($35.8\%$ overall sparsity and $14.5\%$ sparsity on the 62 DKT cortical thickness regions at $k = 3$), squeezing Components $2, \dots, k$ into the remaining parcels ($76.6\%\text{–}81.9\%$ sparsity). We provide two remedies with distinct trade-offs:
   - *Preprocessing remedy (Row-Mean Control + Deterministic ICA):* Subtracting per-subject row means inside each training fold and initializing with deterministic spatial `FastICA` (`initialization_type="ica"`) equalizes sparsity across all columns ($\mathbf{v}_1 = 69.4\%, \mathbf{v}_{2,3} = 65.9\%$) at the $1 - 1/k$ bound, though discarding global atrophy covariance prior to optimization lowers `CogPC1` $R^2$ from $0.1892$ to $0.1408$ ($0.1531$ when the scalar row mean is re-appended).
   - *Constraint remedy (Quantile `sparseness` $\in (0, 1)$, `default=0.5`, operating points `0.5` and `0.8`):* Wrapping `nsa_flow` retraction with column-wise order-statistic soft-thresholding (`DEFAULT_SPARSENESS = 0.5` in `pysimlr`, inherited universally across all linear, deep, flow, and `sklearn` algorithms) strips the diffuse global-mean tail off $\mathbf{v}_1$ without removing subject row means. Following @avants2021, $q = 0.50$ and $q = 0.80$ serve as the two canonical operating points ($61.5\%$ and $81.9\%$ $\mathbf{v}_1$ sparsity under $\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$, or `CogPC1` $R^2 = 0.1968$ at signed $q = 0.50$), while `sparseness = 0.85` achieves exact $(9, 9, 9)/62$ active DKT regions per component ($\mathbf{v}_1 = 85.5\%$ sparse, $\mathbf{v}_{2,3} = 89.2\%$ sparse) and raises `CogPC1` $R^2$ to $0.1923$ ($\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$) and $0.2089$ (`positivity="either"`, $q = 0.70$) (@tbl-quantile-sparseness, @fig-adni-anatomical-heatmap).

## Methodological Principles for Clinical Multi-View Integration

Our experiments highlight four practical rules for clinical multi-view modeling:

* **In-fold covariate adjustment, row-mean control, and completeness hygiene:** Standardizing features, filtering columns below $98\%$ completeness, residualizing demographic covariates (`AGE`, `PTGENDER`, `PTEDUCAT`), and separating per-subject row means strictly inside each training fold prevents test leakage and prevents global size effects from dominating the leading basis column.
* **Bipartite graph topologies when a supervisory battery is absent at deployment:** In `ADNI-MCI`, aligning the three structural MRI views only with each other allows global intracranial and aging variance to dominate the leading components (`PCA` `CogPC1` $R^2 = 0.1522$). Routing training alignment between the MRI views and the 11-scale cognitive battery via a bipartite graph steers the MRI loading matrices $\mathbf{V}_0, \mathbf{V}_1, \mathbf{V}_2$ onto cognitive atrophy patterns while requiring only structural MRI at test time (`CogPC1` $R^2 = 0.2377\text{–}0.2520$).
* **Keeping non-linear capacity downstream of a linear encoder (`LEND` vs.\ `NED`/`NEDPP`):** Placing MLP layers in the decoder (`LEND`, consensus rank $3.33$) captures non-linear generative mappings while preventing the encoder overfitting that degrades `NED` (consensus rank $6.25$) and `NEDPP` (consensus rank $7.12$).
* **Detaching Gaussian prior gradients at rectangular OLEE boundaries (`Flow-SiMR-V`):** When an invertible normalizing flow operates on $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ with $k \ll p_m$, detaching $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}$ in the Gaussian prior log-likelihood prevents the quadratic prior term from rotating $\mathbf{V}_m$ onto trailing noise eigenvectors.

## Limitations and Negative Findings

1. **Statistical parity among top OLEE variants on small block counts:** While the block-level Friedman test across the $B = 12$ datasets is significant on both $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ ($\chi_F^2 = 29.51, p = 2.58 \times 10^{-4}$) and $\mathbf{U}$ ($\chi_F^2 = 16.54, p = 0.0352$), the top cross-view OLEE models (`Flow-SiMR-V`, `LEND`, `SiMLR-LBFGSB`, `SiMLR-LBFGS`, `SiMLR`) lie within the Nemenyi critical difference ($CD = 3.468$).
2. **Equivalence with `PCA` on two-view tabular cohorts:** On low-dimensional two-view cohorts (`Heart`, `Diabetes`) and high-signal `MultiOmics` ER classification, single-matrix `PCA` and `NSAFlow-PCA` perform on par with multi-view alignment at a fraction of the compute cost ($0.003\text{–}0.055\text{ s}$ vs.\ $0.5\text{–}9.6\text{ s}$).
3. **Trade-off between row-mean removal and quantile `sparseness`:** In `ADNI-MCI`, removing the subject row mean prior to optimization equalizes sparsity at $1 - 1/k = 66.7\%$ but lowers `CogPC1` $R^2$ ($0.189 \to 0.141\text{–}0.178$) because global parenchymal atrophy carries genuine cognitive signal; conversely, using quantile `sparseness` ($q \in [0.70, 0.85]$) on column-centered data preserves `CogPC1` $R^2$ ($0.192\text{–}0.209$).
4. **Consensus averaging dilution ($\mathbf{U}$ vs.\ $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$):** On `ADNI-MCI` and `mfeat`, predicting from concatenated per-view projections $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ ($0.2520$ for `LEND`, $0.2377$ for `Flow-SiMR-V`, $0.967$ for `NEDPP`) outperforms predicting from the unweighted 3-dimensional consensus $\mathbf{U}$ ($0.1934, 0.2064, 0.633$). Equal averaging across views dilutes modality-specific predictive power when individual views measure distinct anatomical or geometric scales.
5. **First-order plateauing on non-negative sparse support recovery:** Without quasi-Newton curvature updates, first-order `SiMLR` plateaus early on `NonnegParts` and `NonnegPartsWeak` ($D = 0.183$, $\text{Support } F_1 = 0.495$), whereas bound-constrained `SiMLR-LBFGSB` reaches $D < 10^{-8}$ and $F_1 = 0.991$.
